title: Compex Legal Services Reviews
summary: A 2026 review of Compex Legal Services for plaintiff firms, covering its published turnaround, Asabell, and integrations, and how Codes Health compares on completeness verification and flat fee pricing.
body_markdown:
Medical record retrieval delays stall case timelines, burn paralegal hours, and weaken settlement positions. For personal injury and medical malpractice firms looking at Compex Legal Services, it helps to see the full landscape before committing to a vendor. This review walks through what Compex offers alongside AI-powered alternatives like[Codes Health](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) , so legal teams can make a real decision about their record workflows.


## **Key Takeaways**


-


Compex Legal Services reports more than 50 years of operation, serving more than 5,000 law firms and more than 350 insurance carriers


-


Compex publishes an average turnaround of roughly 15 to 20 days for authorization-based retrieval and about 30 days for subpoena requests, and it advertises real-time tracking, an online portal, and SmartAdvocate integration


-


[Codes Health](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) works toward complete records in a couple of weeks while providing human-verified chronologies and insights on flat fee pricing


-


Codes Health identifies incomplete or defective authorizations as a leading preventable cause of rejected and delayed requests, and its AI validates each request before submission


-


Missing Record Review cross-references delivered records against the original request and known patient history to catch documentation gaps before they surface at trial


-


Services promising same-day retrieval often return only what is immediately available electronically, which Codes Health says pulls clients back into the process and contributes to churn


## **Redefining Medical Record Retrieval for Legal Services**


Medical record retrieval sits underneath every personal injury, mass tort, and medical malpractice case. The work means gathering clinical documentation, billing records, and imaging from hospitals, physicians, specialists, and ancillary providers. Across the retrieval industry as a whole, a lot of that still runs on fax, phone calls, and manual follow-up, which is where the months-long timelines come from. Compex, for its part, advertises its own technology-driven portal, provider location database, research tools, and request tracking.


### **The Speed Differentiator in Legal Cases**


Compex Legal Services offers authorization-based retrieval with a 15 to 20 days on average, per its own FAQ. Subpoena-based requests run to roughly 30 days.


Modern retrieval platforms pull from several pathways at once:


-


Electronic claims networks


-


Custodian integrations


-


Proprietary provider networks


-


Patient and provider portals


-


Traditional fax, email, and telephone outreach


Codes Health uses this kind of multi-channel approach to work toward complete records in a couple of weeks rather than months. Worth flagging: Codes Health does not offer same-day retrieval, and its position is that same-day promises usually deliver only the records already sitting in an electronic pipeline. That sends the client and the firm chasing whatever is left, and Codes Health says that added client involvement is a real driver of churn.


### **Comprehensive Record Collection Channels**


Provider connectivity depth drives retrieval success. Firms run into trouble when clients have fragmented treatment histories across facilities, long medical timelines, or a fuzzy memory of where they were treated.


Effective retrieval needs:


-


Facility identification and verification


-


Authorization validation before submission


-


Persistent follow-up across every available channel


-


Completeness verification against the original request


-


Gap identification and resolution


## **Streamlining Litigation Support with AI-Powered Chronologies and Insights**


Raw records show up as thousands of unsorted pages, and turning that into usable case intelligence takes either a lot of paralegal time or real automation.


### **Automated Case Chronology Generation**


AI chronologies organize encounters and billing records sequentially, grouping related visits and surfacing treatment patterns. That shifts review from page-by-page slog to targeted investigation of the events that matter.


Good chronologies expose:


-


Treatment gaps that may indicate non-compliance


-


Missing documentation from known providers


-


Inconsistencies between billing and clinical records


-


Timeline discrepancies needing clarification


Compex offers Asabell, which chronologically organizes records, highlights diagnoses and treatment, and builds structured visit summaries. Compex describes it as source-grounded and reports up to 67% less review time. Firms should ask whether AI outputs receive a human verification layer, since litigation-grade accuracy depends on expert review of extracted information.


### **Extracting Critical Insights for Legal Strategy**


Past organization, extraction engines pull structured data points that matter for case evaluation:


-


Diagnoses and ICD codes


-


Treatment protocols and medications


-


Provider recommendations and referrals


-


Documented pre-existing conditions


-


Missed appointments and care gaps


-


Documented future medical expenses


For medical malpractice work specifically, flagging potential breaches in care during review adds real value. Codes Health provides[breach-of-care flagging](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/compex-legal-services-alternatives) with human verification, so AI-identified issues get expert confirmation before they shape case strategy. These are flags for attorney review, not legal conclusions.


## **The Compex Legal Services Edge: Experience and Reach**


Compex has operated for more than 50 years and describes itself as the longest-operating national firm in the space. That tenure brings some advantages:


-


Established provider contacts nationwide


-


Proven operational processes


-


Integration with SmartAdvocate case management, where customers can order, track, and receive records


-


Additional litigation support including court reporting, IME coordination, medical canvassing, and social media canvassing


-


Advertised real-time updates on record requests through its online platform


The useful comparison, then, is not whether Compex has technology. It is which documented features each vendor brings to the two places retrieval actually breaks: authorizations that get rejected, and record sets that come back incomplete.


### **How AI and Human Expertise Drive Speed**


Pairing AI automation with human verification addresses both speed and accuracy. Pure AI risks black-box output that legal teams cannot fully trust for litigation. Pure manual process gives up the efficiency automation provides.


[Codes Health](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) markets its approach as AI insights verified by humans, combining:


-


Automated document processing and data extraction


-


Medical professional review of clinical interpretations


-


Legal specialist validation of case-relevant findings


-


Quality assurance before delivery


## **Seamless Integration: Codes Health within Filevine for Legal Teams**


Workflow integration determines how much administrative weight retrieval puts on your team. Standalone vendor portals mean separate logins, manual data transfer, and reconciling case files across systems.


### **Beyond Integration: A Premium Embedded Service**


On July 13, 2026, Filevine announced a strategic partnership with Codes Health that embeds medical record retrieval directly into the Filevine case management environment. The integration lets legal teams:


-


Submit record requests from within the relevant case file


-


Track request status without leaving Filevine


-


Communicate with the Codes Health team through the case workflow


-


Receive completed records and billing directly in the project


-


Review retrieval history and completeness status in one location


Filevine CEO Ryan Anderson described medical record retrieval as a long-standing customer pain point.


### **Maintaining Workflow Continuity**


The embedded approach cuts the context switching that scatters staff attention across systems. Instead of juggling separate portals, communication channels, and billing processes, Filevine firms keep retrieval inside the case management system they already use.


For high-volume customers, Codes Health can also build custom integrations with CRM platforms and other medical software, extending that continuity to firms on different case management systems.


## **Proactive Error Prevention and Verified Completeness**


Codes Health identifies incomplete or defective authorizations as a leading preventable cause of rejected and delayed record requests. When a provider rejects a request, the firm has to correct and resubmit it, restarting a response period that federal HIPAA rules generally set at up to 30 calendar days for qualifying individual access requests, with state deadlines varying.


### **Catching Issues Before Submission**


AI-assisted validation reviews requests before they go out, automatically flagging:


-


Missing or incomplete signatures


-


Invalid or missing expiration information


-


Misspellings in patient or provider information


-


Incomplete permissions required for particular record categories


-


Incorrect provider details or addresses


-


Missing dates of service


This proactive error prevention catches defects that would otherwise come back as provider rejections. When authorization problems only surface after submission, the rejection forces a restart of the whole request.


### **Ensuring Complete and Accurate Record Sets**


Past preventing submission errors, completeness verification compares returned materials against the original request and known patient history. That surfaces:


-


Missing facilities where the patient received treatment


-


Date ranges not covered by returned records


-


Absent billing records needed for damages calculation


-


Documentation gaps that could weaken the case


Codes Health's[Missing Record Review](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/compex-legal-services-alternatives) cross-references patient medical history against the delivered set, flagging documentation gaps before records reach the legal team, then works with facilities to close them.


## **Comprehensive Market Reach: Serving Diverse Legal Practice Areas**


Retrieval needs shift across practice areas, though the core requirements hold steady. Platforms in this space serve:


-


**Personal injury firms** needing records for case qualification, damages documentation, and demand preparation


-


Mass tort practices running similar workflows across large plaintiff portfolios


-


Medical malpractice specialists needing detailed chronologies for expert review


-


Workers' compensation attorneys gathering treatment history for claim support


-


Disability law practices compiling medical evidence for qualification determinations


-


Insurance litigation teams documenting treatment timelines


-


Wrongful death attorneys collecting comprehensive decedent medical histories


Compex reports serving more than 5,000 law firms and more than 350 insurance carriers across these areas. Codes Health, founded in 2024, says it serves hundreds of firms across personal injury, mass tort, and medical malpractice, and it is backed by investors including Y Combinator, General Catalyst, Haystack, Night Capital, and Pathlight Ventures.


## **Beyond Retrieval: Persistent Follow-Up and Visibility**


Provider responsiveness varies enormously. Some facilities turn records around quickly; others need repeated outreach through several channels before anything moves.


### **Ensuring Delivery Through Continuous Outreach**


Persistent follow-up runs through:


-


Phone calls to medical records departments


-


Fax transmission and confirmation


-


Email correspondence with designated contacts


-


Portal submissions where available


-


Escalation for unresponsive facilities


AI-enabled platforms automate much of this, keeping outreach consistent without pulling law firm staff into it. Codes Health's[automated daily follow-up](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/compex-legal-services-alternatives) continues until records arrive or the request needs specific intervention.


### **Real-Time Tracking for Informed Decisions**


Visibility into request status lets teams plan timelines and staffing instead of waiting on periodic vendor updates. Codes Health provides real-time status updates on active requests, including visibility into each fax and call, along with communication logs showing outreach history.


For Filevine users, that visibility lives in the case file, so nobody has to log into a separate vendor system for a status check.


## **The AI-Human Hybrid: Verified Insights for Legal Advantage**


Legal teams are right to hesitate before relying on unverified AI output for case-critical decisions. Accuracy, hallucination, and misread medical terminology are legitimate concerns.


### **Combining Technology with Expert Review**


The hybrid model puts AI in the processing layer and humans in the verification layer:


-


AI processes documents at scale, extracting structured data


-


Medical professionals review clinical interpretations


-


Legal specialists validate case-relevant findings


-


Quality assurance confirms accuracy before delivery


Codes Health describes the overall service as combining elements of a nurse, paralegal, and assistant in one workflow.


## **Compex Legal Services Reviews: What Legal Professionals Are Saying**


Public review data on retrieval vendors is thinner and noisier than most buyers expect, and ratings move, so anything you read should be checked directly before you rely on it.


### **The Public Record on Compex**


The most commonly cited public data point for Compex is its employee review score, which currently sits at 3.2 out of 5 based on 186 workplace reviews as of August 2026. Those are employee reviews, not client reviews, so they say something about working at Compex and nothing measurable about customer satisfaction with retrieval.


Consumer review platforms carry a handful of Compex listings tied to individual office locations, with ratings that differ by location and shift over time. Check the specific profiles directly rather than treating any single aggregate figure as current.


### **Industry Endorsements and Strategic Partnerships**


For newer entrants, partnership validation carries weight. The Filevine partnership puts Codes Health inside one of the legal industry's established case management ecosystems, which provides distribution and a trust signal alongside direct customer testimonials.


Filevine's announcement describes Codes Health as addressing a workflow its customers had been requesting for years.


## **Secure and Compliant Record Handling: HIPAA and Beyond**


Retrieval involves protected health information under strict regulatory requirements, and HIPAA compliance is not optional for a vendor handling patient medical data.


### **Ensuring Data Privacy in Medical Record Processes**


Both Compex Legal Services and Codes Health publicly represent their relevant platforms as HIPAA compliant. Compex describes TruRetrieve as HIPAA compliant and says protected health information is handled under business associate agreements. Codes Health states its platform is fully HIPAA compliant.


Rather than assuming a specific control set, ask each vendor directly for the applicable business associate agreement and current security documentation. Firms with additional security requirements should also ask for current SOC 2, ISO 27001, or other applicable attestations and confirm what each vendor actually holds.


### **Streamlined E-Signature and Document Management**


Authorization management needs secure signature handling. HIPAA-compliant e-signature capability supports:


-


Electronic execution of releases of information


-


Physician order signatures where required


-


Authorization form completion with validation


-


Secure document storage


That electronic workflow removes the delay of collecting physical signatures while keeping the process inside healthcare privacy requirements.


## **Why PI Firms Use Codes Health for Retrieval and Review**


Plaintiff record work fragments quickly. One party requests the records, someone else has to determine whether what came back is complete, and a paralegal ends up holding the whole thing together. Codes Health consolidates that into one workflow, from authorization through analyzed records.


-


AI validation of authorizations and provider requirements before submission


-


Multi-channel provider follow-up across calls, faxes, emails, and portals


-


Completeness verification against the original request and known treatment history


-


Flat fee pricing


-


Native Filevine integration for firms already working in Filevine


-


Custom integrations with CRM platforms and other medical software for high-volume customers


General AI platforms like ChatGPT are not purpose-built for this. They do not provide integrated authorization validation, provider follow-up, Missing Record Review, or the human-verification process that case-critical work requires, and they are not designed for litigation-grade medical record review.


Codes Health's MIT-educated engineering team keeps building out additional workflows and products, so the platform continues to evolve, improve, and become more comprehensive as it meets the changing demands of modern legal practices.


## **Bottom Line**


Compex has been doing this for more than 50 years, and the scale is real: thousands of firms, hundreds of carriers, nationwide provider relationships, plus court reporting and IME work if you want retrieval and litigation support from one place. Its published turnaround of 15 to 20 days on authorization requests is a straightforward number to plan against.


Where Codes Health makes its case is on the two failure points. Authorizations get validated before they go out, and record sets get checked against the original request and known treatment history before they come back to you, with the gaps chased down at the facility. That is also why Codes Health does not offer same-day retrieval. Its position is that same-day delivery usually means only the records already available electronically, which pushes the remaining chase onto your client and your staff, and that added involvement contributes to churn. Complete records in a couple of weeks beats a partial set this afternoon.


[Codes Health](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) pairs that with human-verified AI insights and flat fee pricing, which can make the service fee more predictable across cases with long treatment histories. If your firm runs on Filevine, the whole thing happens inside the case file. Book a demo to see how it handles your actual caseload.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What is the typical turnaround difference between Compex and AI-powered retrieval services?**


Compex publishes an average of 15 to 20 days for authorization-based retrieval and roughly 30 days for subpoena-based requests. Codes Health works toward complete records in a couple of weeks using multiple retrieval pathways, including electronic claims networks, custodian integrations, proprietary provider networks, portals, and traditional outreach, backed by automated follow-up. Actual timelines depend on provider responsiveness and record complexity.


### **Can Codes Health integrate with case management systems other than Filevine?**


Yes. The Filevine partnership provides the embedded integration for Filevine users, and Codes Health can build custom integrations with CRM platforms and other medical software for qualifying high-volume customers. Firms on other systems can discuss options to keep retrieval inside their existing stack.


### **How does flat fee pricing compare to other retrieval pricing models?**


Retrieval vendors use different structures, including per-request, subscription, volume-based, and flat fee arrangements, and what a provider itself may charge for copies is governed separately by federal and state rules depending on the request type.[Codes Health](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) uses a flat fee model, which can make its service fee more predictable across cases involving extensive medical histories or multiple facilities.


### **What happens when retrieved records appear incomplete?**


Missing Record Review cross-references returned materials against the original request and known patient history before the retrieval closes. When gaps turn up, the service works with facilities to resolve the missing documentation rather than handing over whatever arrived. That verification helps firms know the file is complete before case development moves forward.


### **Are there limitations to what AI can accurately extract from medical records?**


General-purpose AI tools are not built for end-to-end medical record retrieval and litigation review. They do not provide the integrated authorization validation, provider follow-up, Missing Record Review, retrieval workflow, and human verification that this work requires, and they are not designed for litigation-grade medical record review. Codes Health's hybrid model pairs AI extraction with medical and legal professional review before findings reach the firm.
